points.title: Role restrictions in the 'who' column cannot be told apart without authentication
points.quote: | correct a project | staff | the project with the new name, address or customer |
behaviours: Treat 'who' as documentation only: any caller on loopback/private network may correct and archive projects, because nothing distinguishes staff from a consumer service while OQ-04 is open
Invent a caller distinction now (header, separate port, frontend-only route) so that only 'staff' can correct/archive and consumer services are refused
points.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel / consumer service authors (whether their correct/archive calls succeed) and the owner reviewing who changed a project

points.title: Producer identity ('owner') is self-declared and unverifiable
points.unit: Primary actions / publish an artifact pointer
points.quote: unknown or archived project, unknown type or owner refused (OQ-03)
behaviours: Accept whatever owner name the caller states and check it only against the vocabulary, so any service can publish (and supersede) a pointer in another service's name
Bind the owner to the calling service (by network origin or credential) and refuse a publish whose declared owner is not the caller
points.who_notices: PresuPro, whose latest estimate pointer could be superseded by another caller; Client Portal reading the latest artifact

points.title: Which actors publish artifacts contradicts between sections
points.quote: Cabinet Kernel and the operator also create projects and rooms and publish artifacts.
behaviours: Treat Cabinet Kernel and the operator as producer services for some artifact types and admit their publishes
Admit publishes only from the producer list ('today: PresuPro estimates; planners by name only') and refuse Kernel/operator publishes as unknown owner
points.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and the operator when their publish is refused or accepted

points.title: Which consumer services may create projects and rooms
points.unit: Primary actions / create a project, add a room
points.quote: | create a project | staff, consumer service |
behaviours: Any consumer service (PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet Web mirror) may create projects and rooms
Only Cabinet Kernel and the operator may, as the Actors section says; other consumers are read-only
points.who_notices: The owner, when Client Portal or PresuPro creates stray projects; consumer authors

points.title: Is a customer required at creation
behaviours: Create a project without a customer and let it be set later by 'correct a project'
Refuse a project without a customer, since R0-01 lists the customer reference as part of identity and context always carries 'customer'
points.who_notices: Staff onboarding a project before the customer is known; consumers reading an empty customer in context

points.title: 'List rooms' for an unknown project has no stated failure
points.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order | — |
behaviours: Answer an empty list for an unknown project id
Refuse an unknown project as not found, like every other per-project action
points.who_notices: Consumer services that rely on the list to detect a mistyped project id

points.title: 'Archived only when asked': included alongside active, or alone
points.quote: the projects, archived only when asked
behaviours: When asked, return active and archived projects together
When asked, return only archived projects (a separate archived listing)
points.who_notices: Staff in the Registry frontend looking for an archived project; consumers paging projects

points.title: Does the artifact list include superseded versions, and how is history read
points.quote: Publishing a new version of a type supersedes the previous one; the history stays readable.
behaviours: 'list artifacts' returns every version including superseded ones, which is how history is readable
'list artifacts' returns only published pointers, and history is reachable only by reading a specific version, an action no row of the table carries
points.who_notices: Consumer services that show estimate history or want only the current documents

points.title: Failure of 'list artifacts' when nothing is published
points.unit: Primary actions / list artifacts / read the latest of a type
points.quote: unknown project; no published artifact of that type
behaviours: Both list and read-latest refuse when no published artifact of the type exists
Listing answers an empty list; only 'read the latest of a type' refuses
points.who_notices: Client Portal / Cabinet consumers rendering a project with no documents yet

points.title: Supersession scope: per project and type, or also per owner
points.unit: Primary actions / publish an artifact pointer
points.quote: the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`
behaviours: Supersede the previous published pointer of the same type in the same project regardless of owner
Supersede only the caller-owner's previous pointer of that type, so two owners publishing the same type keep two published pointers (relevant if OQ-03 lets a type have several owners)
points.who_notices: Consumers calling 'read the latest of a type' and getting one or another owner's document

points.title: R0-04 defers to OQ-08, but OQ-08 does not cover validate/context
points.quote: keeps both answers field for field unless the owner decides otherwise under OQ-08.
behaviours: Freeze validate and context unconditionally, since OQ-08 only asks about bare-array lists and the nested project id
Treat validate/context shapes as open under OQ-08 and reshape them with the rest of the wire
points.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which pin those field names

points.title: Which consumers' reads are contracts besides PresuPro and Client Portal
points.quote: PresuPro and Client Portal read `validate` and `context` and pin their field names.
behaviours: Only those two answers for those two consumers are frozen; Cabinet Kernel and the Cabinet Web mirror may be broken
Every answer any listed consumer reads (Kernel, Web mirror, frontend, onboard_object) is held stable
points.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and Cabinet Web mirror maintainers after a re-authored release

points.title: Are the frontend and onboard_object inside the product boundary
points.quote: through the Registry frontend or an operator script (`onboard_object`)
behaviours: Re-author the frontend and onboard_object as part of Registry, so their behaviour is specified here
Specify only the HTTP API; the frontend and script are external clients that must adapt
points.who_notices: Staff using the frontend/script; whoever must change them under OQ-08

points.title: Stale snapshots after a correction: no change signal
points.quote: reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back (V1-2).
behaviours: Registry only answers reads; a consumer keeps the old name/address/customer until it reads again on its own
Registry notifies or exposes changes (event, changed-since list) so consumers refresh snapshots
points.who_notices: Client Portal / PresuPro users seeing an old address or customer after staff corrected it

points.title: What moves the 'updated' time
points.unit: Primary actions / read a project context
points.quote: id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times
behaviours: Only correct and archive change the updated time
Adding a room or publishing an artifact also changes the project's updated time
points.who_notices: Consumers using the updated time to decide whether their snapshot is stale

points.title: Launch context has no action that produces it
points.quote: Registry gives the launch context (`project_id`, optional `room_id`) and nothing else (V1-3).
behaviours: 'Launch context' is just the ids already returned by read/context; no extra action exists
A separate action returns a launch context (e.g. validates a room belongs to the project) that no row of the table carries
points.who_notices: Downstream services launched with a room_id from another project

points.title: 'Project card' content is unnamed
points.quote: the project card (any status, V1-7) and its rooms
behaviours: The card holds the same facts as the context answer plus rooms
The card carries further stored facts (e.g. artifacts, archive time, customer details) that the context does not
points.who_notices: Staff in the frontend and consumers choosing between read and context

points.title: Which instance a consumer talks to, and why several exist
points.quote: An instance holds its own store. Two instances share nothing
behaviours: One instance per host/environment; each consumer is configured with exactly one Registry
Consumers may reach several instances and must tell projects apart across them, which the document leaves to OQ-02 only
points.who_notices: Operators deploying Registry and consumers resolving a project id
